critical_code_review_comments: employees.py labour_cost: N+1-style — fetches ALL employees + ALL attendance then aggregates in Python. Fine at current seed size (~5 emp × 30 days) but should move to SQL GROUP BY (SUM(CASE status WHEN 'present' THEN 1 WHEN 'half_day' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END)) if project scales to hundreds of workers × year of data.

employees.py attendance upsert: no DB-level unique constraint on (employee_id, attendance_date). Concurrent double-POST could create duplicates due to race between SELECT and INSERT. Add UniqueConstraint on Attendance model + catch IntegrityError to be safe under load.

check_backdate_window uses server-local date.today() with no tz awareness. If server tz drifts from IST the '3-day' window edge cases can flip by ±1 day. Consider explicit tz (Asia/Kolkata) or accept a client-provided timezone hint.
deactivate_employee is idempotent-ish but does not verify e.status != 'inactive' before commit — trivial no-op but avoids audit noise if needed later.
Frontend deactivate uses window.confirm — same UX/test friction called out in iter4; consider shadcn AlertDialog for consistency.
labour_cost amount is null for wage_type != 'daily'; total_amount silently excludes monthly/piece_rate workers. UI should surface a note or aggregate monthly wages pro-rata if needed.
